name: IM-2 Athena
left: Athena lander on its side in a 20 m crater, with the Grace hopper and the MAPP and Yaoki rovers still aboard
fact: Intuitive Machines' second Nova-C lander came down on 6 March 2025 on Mons Mouton, about 160 km from the south pole. Its laser altimeter returned noisy readings all the way down, and the low sunlight confused its crater-matching navigation. Athena hit the surface faster than intended and came to rest on its side in a small crater, its solar panels turned away from the Sun. It worked for under 13 hours, and the hopper and rovers it carried never deployed.
capability: Intuitive Machines calls it the southernmost lunar landing and surface operation yet; NASA received about 250 MB of data from its instruments before the lander went silent.
